title: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
summary:
Negotiations at the COP31 UN climate summit in Turkey are in deadlock and have been suspended for the night, after running more than a day over time, as countries have been unable to agree on a new global climate deal.
The EU and Pacific island nations are amongst a group pushing back against the latest draft agreement which included no reference to reducing the world's demand for fossil fuels.
If countries cannot reach consensus - which is required by the UN's climate talks process - the negotiations could be suspended.
In that case the summit would end with no deal and be reconvened next year.
This has only happened once before since countries started holding COP climate meetings in 1995.

title: This New Study Shows That US Data Centers Use More Power Than These Entire Countries
summary:
As of 2025, the total energy consumption of U.S. data centers exceeded that of some mid-sized countries.
It's staggering to see data center operations equate to entire countries, but it's not altogether surprising when you consider what a data center actually does.
Specifically, the hyperscale data centers mentioned in the Harvard study are used for intensive processes — such as high-density AI training, cloud computing, and storage — and they each house at least 5,000 servers on the low end.
The recent Harvard study shows that the analyzed HDCs also produced up to 31 million tons of carbon dioxide.
With that level of pollution, it's clear that AI data centers may be doing more harm than just driving up utility bills.

title: National Geographic revealed its Pictures of the Year. Here are 8 of the most captivating wildlife photos.
summary:
Out of over 1 million photos taken by National Geographic photographers in 2026, 25 images were named Pictures of the Year.
For its annual year-end issue, National Geographic magazine highlighted the defining photos of the past 12 months, showcasing rare wildlife sightings, split-second nature shots, and how the changing climate is affecting humans and animals alike.
Nathan Lump, editor-in-chief of National Geographic, called the Pictures of the Year collection "a testament to the boundless curiosity and relentless persistence of our photographers in their quest to help us better understand our world."
Here are seven of National Geographic's Pictures of the Year, plus the history-making cover photo.
The entire collection can be viewed on National Geographic's website .

title: united artists for climate calls for art and culture to take stronger role in climate action at COP31
summary:
Artists call for culture in climate policy at COP31For its second edition, United Artists for Climate organizes a collective international campaign inviting artists to share their work, creative practices, and environmental initiatives through Instagram.
A second central demand is to recognize culture as an essential part of climate action and integrate the Culture Global Stocktake into climate decision-making.
The first Culture Global Stocktake was launched at COP31 on November 10th.
The first edition of United Artists for Climate mobilized 290 contemporary artists from 58 countries during COP30 in Belém, Brazil.
By bringing artists into the conversation at COP31, United Artists for Climate argues that culture should not remain on the sidelines of climate negotiations.
